text:
Jess (Support): FYI customer (maya-corp) opened an escalation — streaming responses suddenly slow for their heavy-chat workload. Non-streaming calls are normal. p95/p99 spike for TTFB only. They sent traces + small repro.

Maya (Customer): seeing ~1.2s first chunk now, was ~80ms yesterday. total completion unchanged (~600ms). This breaks our UX because spinner shows longer. Happens on our prod region us-west-2. No code change on our side.

Jess (Support): Repro steps they gave: 
```
# streaming request
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"stream":true,"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# non-streaming
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"stream":false,"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They ran both and compared first-byte time. Attached HAR + small dump.

Carlos (SRE): Can you paste the raw timing headers from the request? We add x-rw-first-chunk-ms and x-rw-total-ms in responses. Also need connection protocol (h2 vs sse).

Jess (Support): Pasting excerpt from customer logs: 
```
Response headers: x-rw-first-chunk-ms: 1207, x-rw-total-ms: 612
Protocol: HTTP/2
Edge: us-west-2-a
Proxy-hop: gateway-2 -> streaming-proxy-5
```

Alex (Eng Runtime): h2 + streaming + proxy in path. We had a recent tiny flush-window tweak in streaming-proxy rolled last night to coalesce small chunks to save bandwidth. That can increase first-chunk TTFB if the model returns small initial tokens. Rolling that back for the affected pools should be an option.

Samir (Oncall): Which commit/rollout? deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-02T03:10Z -> streaming-proxy: coalesce-window=25ms -> succeeded :white_check_mark:.

Alex (Eng Runtime): That aligns. coalesce-window 25ms means proxy collects bytes for 25ms before flush. If customer payloads produce tiny first chunk, that adds latency. Why non-streaming not affected? Because non-streaming waits for end and returns whole payload; first-byte measured is later but consistent.

Carlos (SRE): Short-term mitigation: route maya-corp traffic to a pool with coalesce-window=0 (immediate flush) or mark their route to use SSE fallback which flushes sooner. I can do a traffic rule for their API key.

Jess (Support): Customer asked for workaround asap. Maya, would immediate switch to non-coalescing route be OK?

Maya (Customer): Yes please, low-risk. We'll accept possible small cost bump.

Carlos (SRE): I'll patch the routing config now: adding rule -> match api_key "maya-prod" -> set streaming.coalesce_window_ms=0. Pushing in 2m.

Alex (Eng Runtime): Longer-term: we should make coalescing adaptive based on observed first-chunk latencies per route. Also instrument chunk-size distribution and expose a per-route metric like streaming.first_chunk_size_histogram. Right now we only have counts and p95 first-chunk.

Samir (Oncall): Agreed. Also need an alert for sudden divergence between x-rw-first-chunk-ms and x-rw-total-ms for a route (delta > 300ms). That would catch coalesce regressions quickly.

Jess (Support): Update: Carlos rolled route change -> deploy-bot: traffic-rule update succeeded. Maya, can you confirm if you see improvement?

Maya (Customer): Testing... new traces show x-rw-first-chunk-ms: 65 ms. UI looks fixed. Thanks.

Jess (Support): Great. Customer happy with workaround. We'll keep thread open until eng-runtime ships follow-up.

Alex (Eng Runtime): Action items: 
- Revert default coalesce-window to 0 for customer-tiered routes while we implement adaptive coalescing (owner: Alex).
- Add per-route first_chunk_size_histogram + alert on first_chunk_ms delta (owner: Carlos).
- Add canary fencing: when changing coalesce window, route only 1% traffic for 30m and monitor first-chunk p95.

Samir (Oncall): For rollout safety, also add a runtime flag allowed_by_client that allows customers to opt into coalescing for cost savings. That avoids perf surprises.

Jess (Support): I've opened ticket RW-7821 for the customer-specific routing change and RW-7822 for the adaptive coalesce work and tagged Maya as affected.

Carlos (SRE): I'll keep the routing rule in place for 24h while metrics stabilize, then revert to org default if no regressions.

Alex (Eng Runtime): Preliminary patch idea (pseudo): 
```
if route.coalesce_window_ms > 0 and first_chunk_size < 64 bytes:
  if route.recent_first_chunk_p95 > 200ms:
    set effective_coalesce_window_ms = 0
```
Will PR tomorrow.

Jess (Support): Customer follow-up done. Marking status: mitigated -> workaround applied. Closing once RW-7822 merges.

Maya (Customer): Thanks everyone :pray: very responsive.

deploy-bot: rolling-update complete for traffic-rule maya-prod -> coalesce_window_ms=0
